chapter: Childhood and early career in New Orleans
title: Mrs. Atkin's backyard concerts and the first shows
summary: Neighborhood children sang and danced in concerts, the pay rose, and she moved on to the halls and then to touring shows with her sister.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Mrs. Atkin had a little private catechism school, and most all the neighborhood children attended the school. She used to teach us how to sing and dance. She'd give little concerts on Sundays for the neighborhood, you know, charge 10, 15 cents out in her backyard. They'd build a little, take some wood and build a little platform and get benches and put out there. And most of the whole neighborhood would turn out to see us kids singing, dancing, and go on. And finally, it just got to be such a big thing that everybody started doing it. Pretty in every ward, every now and then, you'd hear of a concert, usually on Sundays and on holidays. And, of course, all the children who were the best were the ones that they would get to come and perform. And then they'd pay us, give us 50 cents, 75 cents. Well, it went up to $1.50, $2.00. Well, we just started, as we started getting bigger and bigger, we started getting bigger pay. Then I started getting offers from the halls, then France Amie Hall, Lekite Hall, Artesian Hall, Hopes Hall, Gloves Hall, Tokyo. Finally, the Dixie Park, the Lincoln Park, then the Pithian Temple, then the Pithian Theater. Then finally, I, well, they just thought I was so good, and they asked me to go away on the shows. And I did. My sister's show. My sister Edna, Benbo, and her husband had a show. So then I left with them, and we was playing all around here in Louisiana. Bugaloosa, Slidell, and my sister was what they used to call a long time ago a coon-shouter. About when was that? Well, I was the, as I started up, I started out, when I made my first communion. I was singing, I was then singing little concerts before I made my first communion. It was during my catechism class that I started, you know, small child.
